## A 9-day wine tour of Argentina and Chile

The [Ada Tours wine itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) lasts **9 days and 8 nights** and crosses two countries: Argentina and Chile. First you explore [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and gaucho traditions, then travel to [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) and the wineries of the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/). The final section includes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) and [Concha y Toro](/chile/place/concha-y-toro/).

This tour suits travelers interested in wine, food and cities: winery visits alternate with theatrical tango, the pampas and time beside the Pacific Ocean. If you want to spend every day exclusively at wineries, examine the itinerary in advance: some sightseeing days are devoted to the history and culture of the two countries.

## Nine days: from tango to vineyards

| Days | What's planned |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Buenos Aires and gauchos |
| 3–5 | Mendoza, Uco Valley |
| 6–8 | Santiago and the coast |
| 9 | Departure from Santiago |

Day one includes a city tour of Buenos Aires. On day two, the itinerary introduces the Susana ranch, gaucho horseback traditions and an evening tango show. This is a separate cultural part of the trip, offering a taste of Argentina before heading toward the vineyards.

On day three, travelers fly to Mendoza and explore the city. Day four is dedicated entirely to the [Uco Valley wineries](/argentina/place/uco-valley/): the itinerary includes visits to three wineries to learn about growing grapes, winemaking and tasting; lunch is provided at one of them. Uco lies south of Mendoza in the Andean foothills. According to Argentina's tourism portal, the wine region encompasses Tupungato, Tunuyán and San Carlos, with notable grape varieties including Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

Day five in Mendoza is free. You can rest or arrange separate activities, but should not assume that every optional tasting is already included in the tour price.

## Santiago and Chilean wine

Day six includes a flight to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and city sightseeing. Day seven introduces [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/), their hills, port and coastal neighborhoods.

Day eight is devoted to the [Concha y Toro](/chile/place/concha-y-toro/) vineyards near Santiago, in the Pirque wine district. The itinerary describes a walk through the vines, the park and a tasting of several wines; lunch on site is offered separately. This Chilean wine stop highlights another production region and complements the introduction to Argentine Malbec.

## Guides, transfers and budget

The [published tour page](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) specifies 8 nights' accommodation with breakfast. Transfers in Buenos Aires and Santiago are private and without a guide, while transfers and excursions in Mendoza, as well as excursions in the capitals, are group services with English-speaking guides. Russian-speaking guides or interpreters can be booked for an additional charge; changing from a group to a private format also requires separate agreement and payment.

International and domestic airfares are excluded from the price. Additional expenses also include tips, personal purchases and optional excursions. When comparing two wine tours, look beyond the per-person price to the number of included tastings, guides, flights and overnight stays.

## Who will enjoy this format

This route is ideal for a first combined journey through Argentina and Chile if wine is important to you but you also enjoy tango, urban history and the ocean coast. If winemaking is your central interest, start by comparing [food and wine tours](/interests/food-and-wine/) and excursions around [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/).

## Frequently asked questions about the wine journey

### How many wineries are included on the Uco Valley day?

**Three wineries** are scheduled, with tastings and lunch at one. The exact winery names are not fixed in the tour text for that day and should not be treated as guaranteed in advance.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide?

Excursions are accompanied by English-speaking guides. A Russian-speaking guide or interpreter can be arranged at extra cost.

### Are flights between the countries included?

No. Domestic and international air tickets are listed under “Not included.” Travel from Mendoza to Santiago is described as a flight on this itinerary, not as a guaranteed road crossing of the Andes.

## Grand tour of Chile and Argentina with Iguazu: who will enjoy 17 days

This journey combines 3 countries and geographically distant regions. Over **17 days and 16 nights**, guests begin in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), explore central Chile's wine region, travel to [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) and then the [Atacama Desert](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The journey continues through Chilean and Argentine Patagonia, [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), Iguazu Falls and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

The itinerary suits travelers who want to see Rapa Nui's moai, desert highlands and glaciers on one trip, with time for wineries and cities between nature days. It involves many flights. If you prefer exploring one national park slowly on foot, choose a more focused [Argentina tour](/argentina/tour/) or [Chile tour](/chile/tour/).

## How the main sections differ

| Stage | Signature experience |
| --- | --- |
| Central Chile | Wineries and Santiago |
| Rapa Nui | Moai and ancient ahu |
| Atacama | Valley of the Moon and desert |
| Patagonia | Torres del Paine and glaciers |
| Mendoza | Vineyards at the foot of the Andes |
| Iguazu | Both sides of the falls |
| Buenos Aires | Architecture and tango |

Two nights are allocated to [Rapa Nui](/chile/place/easter-island/). One excursion visits ceremonial ahu platforms, the Rano Raraku quarry and the Anakena coast. The moai relate to the history of the island's Polynesian population; Rapa Nui National Park is on UNESCO's World Heritage List. Such a visit requires time at each stop and explanations from a guide, so the island should not be treated as a brief photo break between flights.

After returning to the mainland, the route continues to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The contrast with the island is striking: dry high-altitude air, rocky valleys and considerable temperature changes between afternoon and evening. The Valley of the Moon visit allows time for sunset, but a flight south is also listed on day seven. The order and actual timetable for these two activities must be agreed before booking.

At [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), the program focuses on sightseeing at natural attractions, including Milodón Cave, lakes and viewpoints. A private flight then takes guests to Argentine [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), from where they visit [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in Los Glaciares National Park. Views of the glacier face are available along land-based observation routes. More demanding glacier activities and helicopter flights are separate options, not standard inclusions.

## Why combine Chilean wineries and Mendoza in one journey?

The two wine regions allow guests to compare neighboring countries without taking a separate food-and-wine trip. Central Chile includes a day of tastings, while a stay at VIK Chile is associated with the Millahue Valley. The specific wineries for that day depend on the agreed schedule; mentioning several Chilean valleys does not mean they will all be visited.

[Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) includes two nights and a separate day in Luján de Cuyo with visits to three wineries. Proximity to the Andes, climate and grape varieties allow travelers to compare Argentine winemaking with Chile's. More options are available in the [food and wine section](/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Why are there two Iguazu excursions?

The Brazilian and Argentine sides of [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) reveal the same waterfall system from opposite sides of the national border. Panoramic views are the main attraction on the Brazilian side, while the Argentine side offers walking trails and a closer experience of the cascades, including the Devil's Throat area if it is open on the visiting day.

Guests stay on the Brazilian side at Belmond Hotel das Cataratas. After the Argentine-side visit, the itinerary continues to Buenos Aires. Planning must account for entry documents for both countries, the time needed to cross the border and national park opening hours. These depend on travelers' nationalities and the conditions of the particular journey; an Iguazu excursion does not automatically grant entry to both countries.

## What the price includes and how to calculate flights

**The land program starts at $23,700 per person in double accommodation.** It includes 16 nights at the listed hotels and room categories with breakfast, scheduled main excursions, admission tickets and ground transfers. Individual days also list lunches, a boxed lunch, a cocktail and a tango show with dinner. Guiding languages vary by destination: Russian-speaking or English-speaking guides are provided according to the program.

**Private jets between regions are not included in the $23,700.** Charters to Easter Island and Calama, flights across Patagonia and onward to Mendoza, Iguazu and Buenos Aires are calculated separately. Aircraft availability, international permits and dates determine the total quote. International flights to and from the journey, insurance, personal expenses and meals outside the specified program are also excluded from the base price.

It would therefore be misleading to compare this price directly with offers that include scheduled airline tickets. First compare like-for-like service packages. Pay particular attention to transport: it has a substantial effect on the overall budget and the actual pace of travel.

## Climate, luggage and pace: what to prepare

One itinerary covers warm, humid Iguazu, dry Atacama and windy, cool Patagonia. Packing layers is most practical: light clothes for northern sections, windproof and waterproof outerwear, warmer layers for southern viewpoints, comfortable footwear and sun protection. Even with high-end accommodation, some days are spent outdoors in strong winds and bright sunshine.

Easter Island, Atacama and southern national parks may have their own visiting rules. Ada Tours coordinates the sequence of excursions and flights, checks the availability of selected services and helps match border requirements to travelers' nationalities. No fixed departure dates are yet specified for this itinerary, so its route and aviation must be planned as one integrated proposal.

## Frequently asked questions about the grand tour

### Can the tour be booked without private jets?

The main program provides for private aviation sectors, but they are priced separately. Changing the transport arrangements, and the effect on duration, overnight stays and excursions, must be agreed individually before an alternative can be considered equivalent.

### Is a lot of walking required?

The route includes walks through archaeological sites, parks and viewpoint trails. It does not include a multi-day mountain trek. Physical demands should be assessed for each excursion and the accessibility of routes, especially in Patagonia.

### How is this tour different from a journey solely through Patagonia?

Alongside [Chilean Patagonia](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) and Argentine [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), the tour includes Easter Island, Atacama, wineries in two countries and Iguazu. Patagonia occupies only part of the 17 days, but the journey covers many more ecosystems and cultural experiences.

### Is the final total price stated?

No. From $23,700 per person is the land-program price based on double occupancy, excluding private aviation and the other stated exclusions. The final cost depends on dates, aircraft selected and agreed additions.

## “Chile and Argentina VIP”: 26 days through Patagonia, Tierra del Fuego and northern Argentina

Over **26 days and 25 nights**, this program reveals almost the entire range of Argentina's natural landscapes and a substantial part of Chile. It begins in Santiago and on the Pacific coast, crosses Chilean and Argentine Patagonia, Tierra del Fuego, the Valdés Peninsula, the Bariloche lake district and northwestern Argentina, and finishes at Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires.

**The main tour countries are Chile and Argentina.** The program also visits the Brazilian side of Iguazu, while an excursion to Montevideo in Uruguay is offered as an optional extra. When preparing travel documents, consider actual and optional visits rather than relying only on the tour title.

Our VIP itinerary includes private transfers and selected private excursions. The label itself does not promise private aircraft, personal yachts or other services absent from the description.

## From Chile's capital to granite mountains and glaciers

The first days explore [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). The itinerary then heads to [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/) for an extended visit through the national park, including its lakes and granite peaks.

After crossing the Chile–Argentina border, travelers reach El Calafate and visit [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/). These two days reveal Patagonia from different perspectives: Chile's national park offers panoramas of steppe and rugged mountains, while Argentina's Los Glaciares features huge masses of ice and walks near a glacier. The road between them crosses the border, so time for immigration formalities must be allowed.

## Two different days in Tierra del Fuego

In [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), the itinerary includes an off-road trip beside mountain lakes and a separate excursion to Tierra del Fuego National Park. This is a substantial stage, not merely a brief stop at the port. The scenery changes to southern forests, mountain roads and the Beagle Channel coast.

The route then moves to the Atlantic coast, Puerto Madryn and the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/). These days focus on marine wildlife watching. Chances of seeing whales and fur seals depend on the season, weather and animal behavior. When selecting dates, consider how important this part of the itinerary is to you: whale sightings cannot be guaranteed in every month.

## Bariloche's lakes and high-altitude Salta

Around [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/), the tour includes Victoria Island, Arrayanes Forest, the Seven Lakes Route and Circuito Chico. This section features scenic roads, forests and boat excursions. Afterward, the journey shifts sharply to different natural conditions farther north.

[Salta](/argentina/place/salta/) and its surroundings reveal the dry highlands of Argentina: Humahuaca Gorge, Purmamarca, salt flats and Los Cardones National Park. Plan for strong sunshine, possible wind and high elevations at certain stops. Travelers with medical conditions affected by altitude should discuss the journey with a doctor in advance.

## Iguazu Falls and a finale in Buenos Aires

After Salta, a flight takes travelers to Iguazu. The itinerary includes the [Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) of the falls, Macuco Safari, the Bird Park and a helicopter excursion. You will therefore visit Brazil even though the primary tour countries are Chile and Argentina.

The final days are in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), with city sightseeing, tango, a ranch visit and gaucho culture. Extra excursions to Tigre and Montevideo are considered separately; Uruguay is not a guaranteed part of the core trip.

## What's included and what costs extra

The tour includes hotel accommodation with breakfast, private transfers, guide services, admission to national parks and private excursions, except for the separately specified boat trip to Magdalena Island.

**International and domestic flights are excluded from the price**, as are optional excursions, food and beverages during transfers. With such extensive geography, airfare, connections and baggage allowances have a significant impact on the total budget. The VIP label is no substitute for checking the exact list of services.

If you have only two weeks, compare the [14-day “Chile & Argentina Deluxe” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/): it retains Patagonia, Iguazu and Buenos Aires but does not explore Tierra del Fuego, Valdés and northern Argentina in the same depth.

## Frequently asked questions about the route

### What kind of travel does this involve?

It is an extended sightseeing journey with several flights, private transfers and visits to numerous regions. It suits travelers comfortable with frequent hotel changes and varied climates.

### Are Brazil and Uruguay included?

The Brazilian side of Iguazu is part of the actual itinerary. Uruguay is offered as an optional excursion to Montevideo, not a compulsory part of the program.

### Can whale sightings on the Valdés Peninsula be guaranteed?

No. The program includes excursions for watching marine mammals, but seasonal and natural conditions determine the likelihood of sightings.

### Are all excursions strictly private?

Private excursions are included except for the boat trip to Magdalena Island. Optional excursions are arranged separately.

## VIP tour of Chile, Bolivia and Peru: 12 days from Atacama to Machu Picchu

This 12-day itinerary connects three countries of the Andean region. It begins in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), continues into the [Atacama Desert](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), crosses high-altitude Bolivia via the Uyuni Salt Flat, visits La Paz and Titicaca, and finishes in Peru at Machu Picchu and Lima.

Its principal feature is **a continuous crossing of the Andes from south to north**. Long transfers and high-altitude stops are central to this tour, so the VIP label should be judged by the actual route and included services, not taken as a promise of identical hotel comfort at every stop.

## Day-by-day outline: where the major transfers take place

| Days | Region |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Santiago and Atacama |
| 3–5 | Bolivia: Uyuni, La Paz |
| 6–8 | Titicaca, Puno, Cusco |
| 9–10 | Machu Picchu, Sacred Valley |
| 11–12 | Cusco and Lima |

The first five days particularly require careful planning of transport and clothing. After urban Santiago, travelers encounter desert, a border crossing, jeep tracks and a high-altitude city. The second part is more cultural and historical: Titicaca, Andean communities, the Inca valley and the archaeological site of Machu Picchu.

## Atacama and the border crossing into Bolivia

In Santiago, the itinerary introduces the main districts and landmarks of the Chilean capital. A flight then takes the group toward [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) and its desert scenery, including the [Valley of the Moon](/chile/place/moon-valley-atacama/).

Day three includes departure for Bolivia. Stops in this section include Laguna Verde, the Salvador Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, Sol de Mañana geysers and Laguna Colorada. This is a remote natural area with long vehicle journeys between sights, and the weather differs considerably from that of metropolitan Chile.

**Altitude and crossing a land border** are the two main practical considerations. Travel times depend on road conditions, border procedures and weather. The group's entry documents and transfer arrangements should be checked by nationality, without assuming a single rule applies to every traveler.

## Uyuni Salt Flat and La Paz

The next major attraction is the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The white salt plain changes appearance with the seasons: in dry months, its surface patterns stand out, while wetter conditions may create mirror-like reflections in certain areas.

On day five, the journey reaches [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), a large high-altitude city where the cultural part of the Bolivian visit begins. The next excursion heads to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/).

Moving from the salt flat to Titicaca means several consecutive days at considerable elevation. Participating comfortably requires attention to altitude tolerance, cool air and the energy needed even for ordinary sightseeing walks.

## Peru: Titicaca, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu

[Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) hosts the Lake Titicaca program, including the floating [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). The road then continues to Cusco through high-altitude communities.

Day nine includes [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The archaeological site lies among steep Andean slopes and is subject to special conservation rules. Entry depends on the ticket purchased and the permitted visiting route.

Day ten continues into the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). The region includes Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Chinchero and Moray; the specific visits depend on the confirmed itinerary for that day. The journey then continues to Lima and concludes.

## What's included and how to calculate expenses

The package includes **hotel accommodation, excursions, transfers, the specified meals and the train to Machu Picchu**. **International and domestic flights** are paid separately, as are optional excursions, food and drinks beyond the inclusions, tips, medical insurance, any required visas and personal expenses.

The current description does not provide one confirmed starting price. A fair comparison with other Andean journeys must therefore account for all flight sectors, the transfers and accommodation included and the actual duration of high-altitude road journeys.

Travelers who mainly want to explore Inca heritage without the Atacama Desert can compare [Peru itineraries](/peru/tour/) and [other multi-country journeys](/multi-country/). This program is distinctive for crossing **three countries and Bolivia's Altiplano**.

## Preparing for the route

Before departure, the most useful checks are baggage allowances on regional flights, rules for crossing two international borders and weather on high-altitude roads. Sun protection is necessary during the day, with warm clothing for mornings and evenings. Comfortable shoes with reliable soles are advisable.

Do not plan this trip as an uninterrupted luxury retreat: several major sights are far from large towns. In return, one itinerary covers different Andean landscapes—Chile's desert, Bolivia's salt flat and volcanic lagoons, Lake Titicaca and Inca heritage.

## Frequently asked questions about the Chile–Bolivia–Peru tour

### How long does the itinerary last?

**12 days and 11 nights**, beginning in Santiago and finishing in Lima.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Both international and domestic flights are listed among additional expenses in this program.

### Does the route visit Uyuni Salt Flat?

Yes. After Atacama, the itinerary crosses Bolivia and visits Uyuni before continuing to La Paz and Lake Titicaca.

### How is the Machu Picchu visit arranged?

The published inclusions specify **the train to Machu Picchu**. The exact train class and entry time must correspond to the confirmed program and tickets.

## A 12-day VIP tour of Costa Rica and Nicaragua: how the journey works

This journey through [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) and [Nicaragua](/nicaragua/) combines nature excursions with comfortable transfers and a final relaxing stay beside a crater lake. The first section takes in [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/) and a coffee plantation. In Nicaragua, the journey introduces colonial [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), Masaya Volcano and [Apoyo Lagoon](/nicaragua/place/apoyo-lagoon/).

**The main distinction of this 12-day VIP tour is the private aircraft used to travel to Nicaragua and back to Costa Rica.** It applies to flights between the countries. Nature excursions, volcano visits and hotel transfers still take place by road. The tour price includes the private plane both ways, a Russian-speaking guide on excursions, transport with a driver, admission tickets and accommodation on the specified terms.

This itinerary suits travelers who love natural areas, wildlife watching and active activities, with an opportunity to unwind after a busy week of excursions. The geographically similar but differently organized [13-day “Costa Rica and Nicaragua” tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) focuses on Tortuguero, Monteverde, an overland border crossing and Pacific beaches.

## Costa Rica: Arenal, the Frío River and tropical forests

On arrival in San José, travelers head toward the [Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), where La Fortuna is located. It is a convenient starting point for volcanic landscapes and hot springs.

The following day includes a visit to [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/) and an approximately three-hour river cruise on the Frío. From the boat, visitors may see birds, monkeys, caimans, turtles and other wetland wildlife. Specific sightings depend on time of day, weather and animals' natural behavior; the excursion offers an opportunity to observe wildlife but cannot guarantee particular species.

Another day introduces cacao growing, chocolate-making and a walk along the Los Tucanes trail near Arenal Volcano. This combines botany, local production and landscapes shaped by volcanic eruptions. The itinerary also includes an evening folklore program.

[Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/) in Tenorio Volcano National Park is known for its vivid blue water and forest trails. The itinerary includes a walk to the river and waterfall. Costa Rica's official park authority, SINAC, describes the area as a walking route to natural attractions, so expect a hike rather than a brief roadside stop. Trail conditions and entry rules are checked for the visiting date.

## An active day around Arenal: bridges, canopy and canyoning

A separate day combines hanging bridges, a Sky Tram ride, the Sky Trek canopy experience and canyoning at Lost Canyon. This is the most athletic part of the program. Hanging bridges reveal the forest from above; canopy activities involve traveling along cables between platforms, while canyoning means negotiating waterfall sections with specialist equipment.

**Assess the physical demands and individual restrictions before choosing this day.** Canyoning and ziplining may have fitness, weight, age or health requirements. They cannot be replaced by a blanket promise of access for every traveler; conditions must be confirmed with the specific operator before finalizing the itinerary.

After the active adventures, the route continues to [Doka coffee plantation](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/), where travelers learn about growing, processing and roasting coffee and then taste it. The same day includes [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and La Paz Waterfalls. Access to an active volcano's viewpoints depends on current requirements and natural conditions, so its inclusion on the itinerary does not remove the need to confirm accessibility.

## Private flight and onward journey in Nicaragua

On day seven in Costa Rica, a boat excursion around Tárcoles offers a chance to see crocodiles and birds. After lunch, the group goes to the airport for **a private-plane flight to Nicaragua**, followed by a road transfer to the accommodation area. Dates, airports and the actual schedule are agreed for each journey: the private aircraft does not have a departure time fixed in advance for all tours.

The next day begins Nicaragua's historical section. In [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), visitors see colonial architecture, the main square and churches. The itinerary also includes [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/), the Masaya area and [Masaya Volcano National Park](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/). Nature and city excursions take place on the same day, so discuss the pace and access to the volcanic area in advance.

## Three days at Apoyo Lagoon: why they are included

After the first week of activities, the program includes **3 free days at [Apoyo Lagoon](/nicaragua/place/apoyo-lagoon/)**, with no compulsory excursions. The crater lake and its green shores offer a peaceful finish to the journey.

Day twelve includes a private flight from Managua to San José, after which the travelers return home. This sequence places nature and historical excursions at the start and allows the end of the trip to be free from daily early departures.

| Days | Main section |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Arenal, Caño Negro, Río Celeste |
| 5–6 | Canopy, canyoning, coffee, Poás |
| 7–8 | Private flight, Granada and Masaya |
| 9–12 | Apoyo Lagoon, flight back |

## What the VIP format includes and how to compare offers

The price includes hotel accommodation with breakfast or specially agreed terms, Russian-speaking guides during excursions, transfers with a driver, admission tickets and the private aircraft for flights to Nicaragua and back. **Additional excursions, food and beverages outside the specified inclusions are paid separately.**

A VIP label does not automatically mean a personal yacht, permanent aviation support, unlimited included beverages or personal services everywhere. When comparing itineraries, it is better to look at confirmed transport, accommodation type, sightseeing demands and free days.

The [standard 13-day tour of these countries](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua/) includes [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and beaches around [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/), with the border crossed overland. This VIP itinerary instead emphasizes Arenal nature, specific active experiences, private international flights and relaxation at Apoyo Lagoon.

## Frequently asked questions about the VIP journey

### Is the private plane used every day?

No. The private aircraft is included for the flight from Costa Rica to Nicaragua and the return flight. Volcano, reserve and city excursions involve ground travel.

### Are there free days without excursions?

Yes. Three free days at Apoyo Lagoon are scheduled after the sightseeing day in Nicaragua.

### Are canyoning and the hanging bridges included?

They feature in the main itinerary, but individual restrictions and actual availability must be checked beforehand. Do not assume there are no fitness requirements.

### What language are excursions conducted in?

The tour includes excursions with a Russian-speaking guide. Specific services and assistance on non-excursion days are agreed according to the selected arrangements.

### Can Apoyo Lagoon be replaced with a Pacific beach stay?

That would change the itinerary's structure and should be discussed as a custom modification. On this 12-day VIP tour, the final relaxing stay is specifically at Apoyo Lagoon.
